content: Storage in Cloudmin is a set of named libvirt pools. Storage lists each pool with its type, state, capacity, free space and volumes, and Module Configuration chooses the columns shown for pools and volumes.
title: Storage Pools

content:
The installer prepares a default directory pool and tests it with a volume creation and deletion. Virtual machine creation, extra disks, cloning, snapshots, backups and restore work with directory, filesystem and NFS pools, using QCOW2 or raw files, and with LVM and LVM-thin pools, using raw logical volumes. Imported images, installation media, captured images and copied UEFI variable files always live in a file pool, so keep at least one directory, filesystem or NFS pool active. Mount NFS storage before using it as a pool, and mount remote storage before using a directory on it as a backup destination.
Pools differ in what they can do. Cloudmin checks free space before every disk operation, including full disk capacities and temporary snapshots during clones and backups, and checks output volumes for backing links before using them. Libvirt caches directory entries, so Cloudmin refreshes pools before checks that depend on removed files.
heading: Supported pools today

content: Create Storage Pool on the Storage page registers a directory or an existing LVM volume group. A missing directory is created if its parent exists, and existing files and permissions are preserved. Registering a volume group does not format or erase its disks, and each thin pool in the group appears as a separate storage destination. Use Webmin’s Logical Volume Management module to create and extend volume groups and thin pools. New pools start immediately, and the start-at-boot choice is saved with the registration.
heading: Creating pools

content:
LVM disks reserve their full capacity and are zeroed before use, so a new disk never exposes data from an earlier volume. LVM-thin disks allocate space as the guest writes, so their combined capacity can exceed the pool’s physical space. The pool card shows data and metadata usage; extend the thin pool before either fills, because running out stops guest disk writes. Cloudmin refuses new allocation at 95% data usage or 90% metadata usage, and thin pools must have block zeroing enabled.
Shut down a virtual machine before growing one of its LVM disks; file disks can grow while the guest runs. Converting an image into a logical volume needs free space for a private temporary copy. Native LVM snapshots are described on the Snapshots page.
heading: LVM and LVM-thin pools

content:
Each virtual machine gets a separate writable disk so the source image stays reusable. Extra disks can be added, grown, attached and detached from the virtual machine’s hardware page, and deletion asks which disks to remove with shared-storage checks. Cloud-init seed disks and read-only media are excluded from the usage summaries on the overview, which total writable data-disk capacity and mounted guest filesystem usage rather than equating host allocation with guest usage.
Unused files in local directory pools and unused logical volumes can be deleted from the Storage page after a review step. Host mounts, swap, snapshot volumes and volumes still referenced by a machine, an image or another volume are protected.
heading: Volumes

content:
Unregister Pool removes a directory or parent LVM pool from libvirt after checking for references. Files, logical volumes, volume groups and thin pools remain intact. References from stopped guests, snapshots, imported images or backing disks block removal, as do pending operations and unreadable ownership records. Thin destinations cannot be unregistered separately.
Stop and Unregister on the confirmation page stops an active pool before removing its registration. For LVM, this deactivates every logical volume in the group, including thin volumes. Host mounts, swap, open volumes and external device dependencies block the operation. Data is preserved; register the group again to use it in Cloudmin.
heading: Removing a registration

content:
The command-line reference covers list-pools, list-volumes, list-volume-groups, create-pool, directory pool lifecycle controls, delete-volume and unregister-pool. Removal commands accept --review to show owners and any refusal reason, and require --yes to proceed. They recheck ownership and the reviewed identity before changing storage. Use unregister-pool --pool NAME --stop --review to inspect removal of an active pool, then replace --review with --yes to apply it.
The same operations are available through the JSON API. Reads require host access. Changes and reviews also require manage access, a signed token and a writable session. These operations finish synchronously.
heading: API and CLI

content: Local directory pools with QCOW2 or raw volumes (available) Registered LVM volume groups and their thin pools, with raw guest disks, offline growth and native snapshots (available) NFS shared pools (available for imports, creation, cloning and image capture; not yet tested on every supported host and architecture) Safe adoption of existing iSCSI and SAN volumes Planned Managed iSCSI/SAN and Ceph RBD Planned Pools of other types can be defined with libvirt’s own tools; Cloudmin lists active and inactive registrations. A setup UI that discovers candidates, validates every host and shows which operations a pool supports is Planned .
heading: Support order

content: Open Backups and Restore from the Cloudmin menu, or choose Back up virtual machines from a machine’s actions. Each selected machine gets a separate full archive whose filename includes the guest name, the UTC date and the job ID.
title: Backups and Restore

content:
A full backup archives the virtual machine’s managed disks, whether QCOW2 or raw files or LVM logical volumes, its libvirt definition, UEFI variables for firmware-backed guests and a manifest with checksums. Backups use the same source preparation and recovery as cloning: a stopped source is archived directly, and a running source is frozen through the guest agent and snapshotted, through temporary overlays for file disks or native snapshots with a brief pause for LVM disks, or shut down cleanly if you prefer. A running source with both file and LVM disks needs the clean shutdown. Unlike clones, backups preserve the guest identity and license credentials.
Manual and scheduled backups share the host’s disk-work queue, so only one backup or other queued disk operation runs at a time. Backups pass data through several copies on the way to the destination, so temporary space on the host matters; the page shows the space needed.
heading: What a backup contains

content: Local destinations are private directories, including mounted NFS storage. Cloudmin creates a missing backup directory with private permissions. SSH destinations use SFTP with host key trust: the first connection scans the server’s key and asks you to approve its fingerprint, and later connections require the trusted key. Password and key authentication are supported. S3 destinations work with Amazon S3 and compatible services. Pro Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, Backblaze B2, Dropbox and Google Drive transfers come with the Cloudmin Pro extension and use Virtualmin’s provider helpers. Real-account transfer tests for these providers are still pending. Provider credentials belong in the backup destination settings. Password fields stay empty on edit and keep the saved secret unless you enter a new one.
heading: Destinations

content: Schedules run hourly, daily, weekly, monthly or yearly with a retention count. Cloudmin inspects destinations to apply retention and to list archives for restore, and an hourly inspection cleanup keeps the cache tidy. Scheduled backups appear as jobs like manual ones.
heading: Schedules and retention

content:
Restore verifies the archive before asking for confirmation. It replaces a missing machine with its original identity and refuses to overwrite an existing name or UUID. The restored machine is left stopped with automatic startup disabled, and keeps the hostname, machine ID, host ID, MAC addresses, guest network files, passwords, SSH keys and license files. Restore does not deregister Virtualmin Pro or contact its license service. Use cloning to create another machine with a new identity.
Choose an active directory, filesystem, NFS, LVM or LVM-thin pool for the restored disks. Disks restored into an LVM pool become raw logical volumes. File and ordinary LVM pools need room for the disks’ full capacities plus a margin, while thin pools allocate space as data is restored; local staging also needs space for downloading, extracting and inspecting the archive. UEFI variables are always restored into a file pool.
heading: Restore

content: Backup, backup inspection and restore are API actions with the same job model as creation, so they can be driven from api.pl or remote clients. See Virtual machine API.
heading: API and CLI

content: Scheduled snapshots as a lighter alternative to full backups Planned Fleet backup policy across hosts in Cloudmin Connect Pro Planned
heading: Planned

content:
Planned feature
The legacy import tool described here is a design target and is not available yet. Cloudmin 10 does not upgrade a Cloudmin 9 host in place, and a package upgrade never imports existing virtual machines.
title: Migrating from Cloudmin 9

content: Cloudmin 10 breaks internal compatibility with Cloudmin 9 on purpose, but it must not break user data. Existing KVM installations get a visible, tested import and rollback path, and Cloudmin 9 stays available and maintained for Xen users while the KVM line matures.
heading: Why import is explicit

content:
The importer is a separate tool, never a package side effect:
cloudmin migrate --scan reads the old configuration without changing it and backs up the legacy controller state. It inventories Servers Index records, flat files, running QEMU processes, boot scripts, disks, LVM volumes, iSCSI mappings, bridges, MACs, IPs, console settings, schedules, owners and image references. It produces a report for each virtual machine: Result Meaning Ready Cloudmin can import the virtual machine safely. Review Import is possible, but the administrator must confirm a choice. Blocked Part of the old configuration cannot be translated safely. For each ready virtual machine it generates and validates a libvirt definition without starting it, stops the old virtual machine, disables only its exact legacy start-up entry, defines and starts it through libvirt, runs health checks, and commits only when they pass. If anything fails it undefines the new domain and restores the legacy boot entry. The importer preserves the UUID where known, the name, MACs, disk paths and formats, boot order, CPU, memory, firmware, network attachments and autostart. It reuses disks in place when safe and does not copy old SSH or Webmin passwords. Unsupported QEMU options block with an explanation.
heading: The planned importer Planned

content: Install Cloudmin 10 on a fresh supported host and create new virtual machines there. Keep Cloudmin 9 hosts running; installer and critical compatibility fixes continue on a maintenance branch. Guests defined in libvirt by other tools appear in Cloudmin 10’s inventory; full adoption with Cloudmin management is Planned .
heading: What you can do today

content: Cloudmin Services from Cloudmin 9 is not carried forward. Virtualmin Connect, an optional Webmin module, is Planned to replace it: shared DNS, database, spam and virus services become remote-server settings in Virtualmin, and Connect distributes settings and policy, enforces per-owner quotas and the cross-server subdomain check, and keeps the server list, monitoring and provisioning log. A one-time script to migrate owners, limits and provisioning history from a Cloudmin 9 master is part of that plan.
heading: Cloudmin Services and Virtualmin fleets

content: The web interface, the command line and remote clients share one versioned API for virtual machine creation, power controls, management, cloning, backups, restore and host storage. The UI calls it internally; api.cgi exposes it over HTTP. The cloudmin command uses the same API on the host.
title: Virtual Machine API and CLI

content:
Send a JSON object or form fields with an action. Responses are JSON with version: 1 and either result or error. Always check the error field: Webmin’s CGI server returns HTTP 200 for JSON responses. Actions that make changes require POST and a signed token returned by the options action, which also lists the images, pools, networks, templates and plans available to the caller.
HTTP clients must pass Webmin’s referer check: send a Referer from the same Webmin origin, or use the supported User-Agent: Webmin API convention. Webmin authentication and Cloudmin module permissions apply. Delegated users can call options and use the permitted power and password reset actions on their assigned virtual machine UUIDs.
heading: Requests and responses

content: Action Purpose machines List visible virtual machines or read one by name or UUID options Available images, pools, networks, templates, plans and a form token review Validate a creation request without creating anything; stores only a private password hash for reuse create Create a virtual machine; repeated submissions of one attempt return the same job status, list Read a job or the caller’s recent jobs start, shutdown, reboot, suspend, resume, reset, force_off, autostart Power controls; abrupt actions need confirm reset_password Change a guest account through the guest agent update, add_disk, grow_disk, attach_disk, detach_disk, delete_disk, delete and related actions Offline and live hardware management clone Full clone with a new identity or an unchanged stopped copy backup, backup_inspect, restore Full backups and restore snapshot_create, snapshot_restore, snapshot_delete Disk snapshots capture_image Image capture, with the Cloudmin Pro extension Passwords and license credentials are removed from input before anything is logged or rendered. Review stores a password hash privately for one day, bound to the token, attempt ID, Webmin user and initial username, so a following create can omit password. Responses never contain passwords or hashes.
heading: Actions

content: license returns public license status and accepts GET without a token. check_license refreshes it; change_license takes serial and license_key; deregister_license removes saved license and repository credentials and requires confirm=1. All license actions require host access. Writes also require POST, a signed token and a writable session. These repair actions remain available when licensing blocks new changes. See License Manager for grace periods and the operations that continue after expiry.
heading: Host license

content:
storage returns active and inactive pools, volumes, ownership information, revisions and unregistered LVM groups. It requires host access and allows GET without a token. The following synchronous actions also require manage access, POST, a signed token and a writable session:
Action Purpose register_pool Register a directory or an existing LVM volume group pool_start, pool_stop, pool_autostart Change a directory pool’s state or boot policy using its current revision volume_review, delete_volume Review ownership, then delete one unused volume with its revision and confirm=1 pool_review, unregister_pool Review references, then remove a directory or parent LVM registration with its revision and confirm=1 API pool selectors are UUIDs; volume selectors are exact names within a pool. CLI pool selectors also accept unambiguous names. Unregistration keeps all data. An active pool requires stop=1 in both pool_review and unregister_pool; the review reports stop_required. For LVM this deactivates the whole volume group after checking host use and dependencies. The default stop=0 refuses active pools. See Storage Pools and the command-line reference for usage and limits.
heading: Host storage

content: A creation request names the virtual machine and selects an image or catalogue entry, install_source (cloud or iso), pool, network, cpus, memory_mib, disk_gib, the initial username, auth_type (password, keys or both) with password or ssh_keys, address_mode (dhcp or static) with ipv4, ipv6, gateway4, gateway6 and dns, firmware, start, autostart, an optional hostname and mac, and a template and plan. Software fields are software (none, virtualmin-gpl or virtualmin-pro), virtualmin_bundle, virtualmin_type, virtualmin_postgres, virtualmin_ssl, webmin_register, packages, and the before and after scripts with their modes and paths. Pro creations also take virtualmin_serial and virtualmin_key on each request.
heading: Creation request fields

content: Creation, cloning, backups, restores, captures and hardware changes return a job immediately. A job record carries its state, phase, events, error, cleanup status and, for Virtualmin installations, the URL to open when it completes. Jobs reserve the resources they touch, can be cancelled at safe points, and recover after a controller restart. Job records never expose private request fields.
heading: Jobs

content:
Run cloudmin as root on the Cloudmin host. Commands such as cloudmin list-systems, cloudmin create-system and cloudmin backup-systems share the API’s validation and recovery. Lists use tables by default; add --multiline for details or --json for scripts. Jobs are followed unless --no-wait is supplied.
See the command-line reference for all commands and examples, or run cloudmin help COMMAND. The raw JSON entry points remain available as api.pl and cloudmin api ACTION.
heading: Command line

content: A machine-readable API schema and generated reference documentation Planned Revocable API credentials limited to individual actions, and automation credentials for projects Planned
heading: Planned

content:
Run cloudmin as root on the Cloudmin host. Lists use tables by default; --multiline shows details. --json returns an object with command, status and data fields; data holds the API result. Success exits 0, operation failures exit 1, and usage errors exit 2.
Commands wait for jobs by default; --no-wait returns the job ID immediately. Passwords and license credentials are read from files or standard input.
Each command has its own page with syntax, options and examples. cloudmin help COMMAND shows the same text on the host, and cloudmin COMMAND --help shows the syntax alone.
title: Command Line API

content: list-systems: Lists the virtual machines on this host. get-system: Shows a virtual machine and its saved settings. start-system: Starts a stopped virtual machine. shutdown-system: Shuts down a virtual machine cleanly. reboot-system: Requests a guest operating system reboot. pause-system: Pauses a running virtual machine. unpause-system: Resumes a paused virtual machine. restart-system: Shuts down and starts with the saved settings. reset-system: Resets virtual hardware immediately. poweroff-system: Powers off immediately without a clean shutdown. modify-system: Changes saved resources, boot settings or automatic startup. passwd-system: Changes an existing guest account password through its agent. create-system: Creates a virtual machine from a cloud image or installer ISO. clone-system: Copies a virtual machine to independent disks. delete-system: Deletes a virtual machine and only the selected disk targets.
heading: Virtual machines

content: list-disks: Lists a virtual machine’s disks and removable drives. create-disk: Creates and attaches a disk. attach-disk: Attaches an unused storage volume. detach-disk: Detaches a disk while keeping its data. delete-disk: Detaches and permanently deletes one disk. resize-disk: Grows a disk to the specified total capacity. insert-media: Inserts an ISO in an existing CD/DVD drive. eject-media: Ejects media without removing the drive. list-interfaces: Lists a virtual machine’s network interfaces. add-interface: Adds a virtio network interface. modify-interface: Changes an interface’s network, link or bandwidth. delete-interface: Removes a network interface.
heading: Disks and interfaces

content: list-snapshots: Lists snapshots for the host or one virtual machine. create-snapshot: Creates a disk snapshot. restore-snapshot: Restores a saved snapshot. delete-snapshot: Deletes a snapshot while keeping current disk data.
heading: Snapshots

content: list-backups: Lists completed backup archives. backup-systems: Creates a full backup of one virtual machine. inspect-backup: Verifies a backup archive before restoring it. restore-systems: Restores an inspected backup with its original identity.
heading: Backups

content: list-images: Lists imported and catalogue images. list-networks: Lists usable virtual networks and host bridges. get-host: Shows host capabilities. create-image: Creates a reusable image from a virtual machine (Cloudmin Pro).
heading: Host and images

content: list-jobs: Lists recent and unfinished jobs. get-job: Shows a job’s current progress. cancel-job: Requests cancellation at the next safe point. recover-job: Resumes interrupted work or retries cleanup. discard-job: Keeps completed disk growth and discards the remaining failed edits.
heading: Jobs

content: list-pools: Lists active and inactive storage pools. list-volumes: Lists storage volumes and their owners. list-volume-groups: Lists LVM volume groups available for registration. create-pool: Registers a directory or an existing LVM volume group. start-pool: Starts a directory pool. stop-pool: Stops a directory pool without deleting its files. set-pool-autostart: Changes whether a directory pool starts at boot. delete-volume: Deletes an unused storage volume after a review. unregister-pool: Removes a pool registration and keeps its data.
heading: Host storage

content: Cloudmin’s page handlers run as root, like other Webmin modules, but the risky work does not. Image and provisioning tools, consoles and relays run as separate processes without root privileges, even when the administrator is logged into Webmin as root.
title: Privilege Separation

content: Webmin, Cloudmin’s CGI scripts, the command line, the status collector and the controller jobs. They use normal Webmin initialization, authentication and permission checks, validate form tokens and input, record progress and make the libvirt changes. The module never installs host packages from a page request; cloudmin-install and Cloudmin-Config prepare the host.
heading: What runs as root

content:
Downloads, host-file reads, checksum checks, disk inspection, SSH key validation, cloud-init seed generation, clone preparation, backup archive handling and transfers, guest software monitoring, and the console and terminal relays. Systemd assigns each task a temporary user ID through DynamicUser and releases it when the task stops; no permanent account is created.
Each worker starts as a fresh Perl or Python process without inheriting Webmin’s memory, environment, open files or libvirt connections. It has private files, no Linux capabilities, a read-only view of the system, and no access to Webmin’s credential files or libvirt control sockets. Download and size-lookup tasks receive Webmin’s outgoing proxy settings, including proxy credentials when configured, in a private request file. Host-file reads, compatibility inspection, key validation and seed generation also have no host network access.
Libguestfs workers receive a private kernel copy from the root controller, so host kernel permissions stay unchanged, and need access to /dev/kvm through the kvm group. Installation readiness boots a real isolated KVM appliance the same way.
heading: What runs without root

content: A root supervisor prepares each console or terminal connection, checks the session’s permission, hands the relay only its prepared sockets and private credentials, and handles cleanup. The relay speaks WebSocket to the browser and SSH or VNC to the guest; the SSH client runs inside the relay’s unit with the guest’s pinned host key and the selected managed key delivered as a systemd credential. The supervisor rechecks the session’s grant every five seconds and closes the connection when it is revoked. Serial consoles forward bytes between the libvirt stream in the supervisor and the relay, keeping the management connection out of the relay.
heading: Interactive relays

content: Cloudmin’s root process checks permissions and input before applying network changes through libvirt and Webmin’s network backends. Task workers cannot change host networking. Cloudmin does not need passt or slirp4netns.
heading: Networking privileges

content: Workers require systemd 247 or later, systemd-run and working nss-systemd user lookup. If a worker cannot start with these restrictions, the operation fails; it never falls back to running the tools as root. A host-file import must be readable without root; use a browser upload for a private file. This design does not change the host to qemu:///session or replace its existing virtual networks.
heading: Requirements and limits

content: Guest passwords are hashed for cloud-init and the hash is removed from the job record when creation finishes. Virtualmin Pro credentials are removed once the guest accepts them. Console passwords, Servers Index logins and backup destination secrets are kept out of job logs, process arguments, audit records and Webmin’s file-change logs. Managed SSH private keys stay in Cloudmin’s private module data directory with mode 0600.
heading: Secrets

content:
cloudmin list-systems [--multiline | --json] [--name-only | --id-only] [--name name]* [--id uuid]* [--state running|stopped|paused] [--template ID|name] [--plan ID|name] With no filters, lists the virtual machines visible to the caller, ordered by name. The default table shows each machine’s name, power state, CPU count, memory allocation and known IP addresses.
Use --name or --id to select exact names or UUIDs. Repeat either option to select several machines. Multiple values of the same option are alternatives; different filters must all match. For example, two --name options with --state running show only the named machines that are running. An empty result means no machines matched.
--state accepts running, stopped or paused. --template and --plan accept an existing preset’s ID or unambiguous name and match the recorded creation preset. They do not compare the machine’s current settings with the preset.
Use --multiline to see details including UUID, disk capacity and automatic startup. A disk capacity that could not be measured is unknown, not zero. --json returns structured data for scripts. --name-only and --id-only print one name or UUID per line, without a heading.
cloudmin list-systems cloudmin list-systems --state running --multiline cloudmin list-systems --name web.example.com --name db.example.com \ --id-only cloudmin list-systems --plan "Default Plan" --json Options:
--name name: Exact virtual machine name. --id uuid: Exact virtual machine UUID. --state running|stopped|paused: Power state. --template ID|name: Template ID or name. --plan ID|name: Plan ID or name.
heading: Lists the virtual machines on this host

content:
cloudmin get-system [--multiline | --json] (--name name | --id uuid) Select one virtual machine with --name or --id. The result combines its inventory summary with its saved configuration, including resources, disks, network interfaces and boot settings. Use list-systems to find its name or UUID.
For a running machine, the result also includes running resource settings and any differences from the saved settings. Pending changes take effect after a full shutdown and start; an operating system reboot may not apply them. Use restart-system to perform that full restart.
--multiline expands nested details, and --json returns the complete structured result. For a shorter view of attached devices, use list-disks or list-interfaces. This command reads settings once; it does not monitor changes.
cloudmin get-system --name guest.example.com --multiline cloudmin get-system --id MACHINE_UUID --json Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Shows a virtual machine and its saved settings

content:
cloudmin start-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) Select a stopped virtual machine with --name or --id. It starts with its saved hardware configuration, applying settings that were waiting for the next start. This command does not change whether the machine starts automatically when the host boots; use modify-system --autostart yes for that.
By default, waits up to two minutes for the host to report the machine running. That state does not mean the guest operating system, network, cloud-init or software installation is ready. --no-wait returns once the start request is accepted. It does not return a background job ID.
Use unpause-system for a paused machine. An unfinished operation can prevent starting a guest; check list-jobs before repeating a refused request.
cloudmin start-system --name guest.example.com cloudmin start-system --id MACHINE_UUID --no-wait Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Starts a stopped virtual machine

content:
cloudmin shutdown-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) Requests a clean shutdown of the machine selected by --name or --id. The guest operating system must respond to the shutdown request. Its disks, saved hardware settings and automatic startup setting are retained.
By default, waits up to two minutes for the host to report the machine stopped. A timeout fails the command but does not cancel the shutdown request: the guest can still stop later. Cloudmin never turns a timed-out clean shutdown into a forced power-off.
--no-wait returns after the request is accepted. Use get-system or list-systems to check the state later. Use restart-system for a clean shutdown followed by a start, or poweroff-system --yes when a forced stop is necessary.
cloudmin shutdown-system --name guest.example.com cloudmin shutdown-system --id MACHINE_UUID --no-wait Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Shuts down a virtual machine cleanly

content:
cloudmin reboot-system [--multiline | --json] (--name name | --id uuid) Requests an operating system reboot of the running machine selected by --name or --id. This is a clean reboot request; the guest must respond to it. The command returns when libvirt accepts the request, without waiting for the guest to reboot or its services to become ready.
An operating system reboot does not guarantee that pending CPU, memory or boot configuration changes take effect. Use restart-system for a complete shutdown and start with the saved hardware configuration. Use reset-system only when an immediate hardware reset is intended.
cloudmin reboot-system --name guest.example.com cloudmin reboot-system --id MACHINE_UUID --json Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Requests a guest operating system reboot

content:
cloudmin pause-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) Pauses execution of a running machine selected by --name or --id. Its memory and virtual devices remain allocated on the host. This is not a saved state on disk and does not survive stopping the machine or shutting down the host.
The guest cannot process requests while paused. Network connections and application operations may time out. Resume execution with unpause-system; use shutdown-system when the goal is to stop the operating system cleanly and release its resources.
By default, waits for the paused state. --no-wait returns as soon as the pause request is accepted. Neither form creates a background job.
cloudmin pause-system --name guest.example.com cloudmin pause-system --id MACHINE_UUID --no-wait Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Pauses a running virtual machine

content:
cloudmin unpause-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) Resumes execution of a paused machine selected by --name or --id, using its existing memory and running hardware state. It does not boot the operating system again or apply settings saved for the next start.
By default, waits for the host to report the machine running. --no-wait returns after the resume request is accepted. Applications may need to reconnect after the pause, so a running state does not prove that all services have recovered.
Use start-system for a stopped machine. list-systems --state paused finds machines that can be resumed.
cloudmin unpause-system --name guest.example.com cloudmin unpause-system --id MACHINE_UUID --no-wait Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Resumes a paused virtual machine

content:
cloudmin restart-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) Performs a full shutdown and start of the machine selected by --name or --id. Use this to apply saved CPU, memory or boot settings that get-system shows as pending. A guest operating system reboot alone may leave those changes pending.
The operation runs as a background job. If the machine is running, the worker requests a clean shutdown and waits up to two minutes. A timeout fails the job without forcing the guest off or starting it again. A delayed guest shutdown may still finish after the job reports failure.
By default, waits for the job to finish. --no-wait returns its ID for later inspection with get-job. Success means the machine has been started with its saved configuration; it does not wait for guest applications to become ready.
cloudmin restart-system --name guest.example.com cloudmin restart-system --id MACHINE_UUID --no-wait Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Shuts down and starts with the saved settings

content:
cloudmin reset-system [--multiline | --json] (--name name | --id uuid) --yes Immediately resets the virtual hardware of the machine selected by --name or --id. The guest has no opportunity to stop applications or flush pending writes. Unsaved data can be lost. --yes is required to confirm this operation.
Use reboot-system for a clean operating system reboot. A hardware reset does not guarantee that pending saved hardware changes are applied; use a full shutdown and start for those changes.
The command returns when the reset is accepted, without waiting for the operating system or services to become ready. It does not delete the machine or its disks.
cloudmin reset-system --name guest.example.com --yes Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --yes: Confirm this operation.
heading: Resets virtual hardware immediately

content:
cloudmin poweroff-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --yes Immediately stops the machine selected by --name or --id, without asking the guest operating system to shut down. Unsaved data can be lost. --yes is required. Use shutdown-system when the guest can shut down cleanly.
The machine definition, disks and automatic startup setting are retained. Use start-system to start the machine again.
By default, waits for the host to report the machine stopped. --no-wait returns after the forced stop is accepted. This is a power operation, not a background job.
cloudmin poweroff-system --name guest.example.com --yes cloudmin poweroff-system --id MACHINE_UUID --yes --no-wait Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --yes: Confirm this operation.
heading: Powers off immediately without a clean shutdown

content:
cloudmin modify-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--autostart yes|no] [--boot value] [--bootmenu yes|no] [--changes-file file|-] [--cpu-limit number] [--cpus number] [--desc value] [--enable-live] [--memory size] [--memory-limit size] Changes selected settings of the machine identified by --name or --id. Omitted fields keep their existing values. The command reads the current configuration revision before submitting the update, so a conflicting concurrent edit can still cause the request to fail.
Resources and boot settings --cpus and --memory set the allocation. --cpu-limit and --memory-limit set the maximum CPU count and memory, not CPU usage or scheduling limits. Bare memory values use MiB; 4G means 4 GiB.
Supported CPU and memory allocation changes can apply while the guest runs. Allocation changes outside its running limits, changes to resource maximums, and boot settings are saved for the next full shutdown and start. If a supported live change fails, the command reports the error. Check get-system --multiline for running values and pending changes, then use restart-system when needed. Adding CPUs or adjusting memory through ballooning also requires guest support.
--boot disk:vda selects a disk as the first boot device; --boot nic:MAC selects a network interface. This replaces the saved boot order. --bootmenu yes enables the firmware boot menu. Use list-disks and list-interfaces to find device identifiers.
Preparing for live changes --enable-live requires a stopped guest. It adds CPU slots, spare device ports and a CD drive for later changes while preserving the current allocation. The command does not shut a running guest down automatically.
Combined hardware edits --changes-file reads a JSON array of up to 128 disk or interface edits. Each entry uses an API action and its fields, for example grow_disk with target and disk_gib. An existing device can be changed only once in the array. Disk deletion requires the separate delete-disk command.
The whole request is validated before any changes, but disk growth cannot be undone if a later step fails. Use get-job and recover-job for an interrupted update. When its safety checks pass, discard-job keeps completed growth and releases the machine for further edits.
Automatic startup and completion --autostart yes starts the machine when the host boots; --autostart no disables that behavior. If combined with hardware edits, it is changed only after their job succeeds. With --no-wait, submit automatic startup as a separate command.
The command waits for hardware edits by default. --no-wait returns the job ID. Use --json for the job record, including any fields saved for the next start.
cloudmin modify-system --name guest.example.com --memory 4G --cpus 2 cloudmin modify-system --name guest.example.com --boot disk:vda \ --bootmenu yes cloudmin modify-system --name guest.example.com --autostart yes cloudmin modify-system --id MACHINE_UUID --changes-file \ /root/hardware-edits.json Options:
--autostart yes|no: Start when the host boots. --boot value: First boot device: disk:TARGET or nic:MAC. --bootmenu yes|no: Enable the firmware boot menu. --changes-file file|-: JSON array of hardware edits. --cpu-limit number: Maximum CPUs. --cpus number: Number of CPUs. --desc value: Description. --enable-live: Add CPU slots, spare device ports and a CD drive while stopped. --id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --memory size: Memory allocation; bare values use MiB. --memory-limit size: Maximum memory; bare values use MiB. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Changes saved resources, boot settings or automatic startup

content:
cloudmin passwd-system [--multiline | --json] (--name name | --id uuid) --password-file file|- --user value Changes the login password of an existing account inside the machine selected by --name or --id. --user names the guest account, not a Webmin user. The machine must be running with a responding QEMU guest agent. This command cannot create an account or reset a password in a stopped guest.
--password-file reads the new password from a regular UTF-8 text file. --password-file - reads it from standard input. One final newline is removed. Keep password files private; the password itself is never a command-line argument or part of the public result.
The command returns after the agent accepts the change. It does not change SSH authentication policy, unlock other login methods or replace authorized SSH keys. For example, changing a password does not enable SSH password login if the guest disables it.
cloudmin passwd-system --name guest.example.com --user cloudmin \ --password-file /root/guest-password cloudmin passwd-system --id MACHINE_UUID --user cloudmin --password-file \ - < /root/guest-password Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --password-file file|-: Password file, or - for stdin. --user value: Existing guest account.
heading: Changes an existing guest account password through its agent

content:
cloudmin create-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] [--address-mode dhcp|static] [--after-script-file file|-] [--after-script-mode none|file|inline] [--after-script-path value] [--auth-type keys|password|both] [--autostart | --no-autostart] [--before-script-file file|-] [--before-script-mode none|file|inline] [--before-script-path value] [--cpus number] [--desc value] [--disk size] [--dns value] [--firmware auto|efi|bios] [--gateway4 value] [--gateway6 value] [--host-ssh-key | --no-host-ssh-key] [--hostname value] [--image ID|name] [--install-source cloud|iso] [--ipv4 value] [--ipv6 value] [--license-file file|-] [--license-serial-file file|-] [--mac value] [--memory size] --name value [--network ID|name] [--packages value] [--password-file file|-] [--plan ID|name] [--pool ID|name] [--require-fqdn | --no-require-fqdn] [--review] [--software none|virtualmin-gpl|virtualmin-pro] [--ssh-key value]* [--ssh-keys-file file|-] [--start | --no-start] [--template ID|name] [--username value] [--virtualmin-bundle LAMP|LEMP] [--virtualmin-postgres | --no-virtualmin-postgres] [--virtualmin-ssl | --no-virtualmin-ssl] [--virtualmin-type full|mini] [--webmin-register | --no-webmin-register] Creates a new virtual machine named by --name. This name must be unused on the host. The operation runs as a background job; by default the command waits for creation and any selected software setup to finish. --no-wait returns the job ID instead.
Image, storage and resources Use list-images, list-pools and list-networks to find available choices. Image, pool, template and plan options accept an ID or an unambiguous name. A catalogue image uses an ID such as catalogue:IMAGE_ID; Cloudmin downloads or reuses it as needed. --pool selects the destination for the new disk, not the image’s existing location.
--template supplies creation defaults and --plan supplies resource defaults. They are used only when explicitly selected. Command-line fields override their defaults, except that a template’s required fully qualified hostname cannot be disabled. If you omit a required setting without a preset that supplies it, validation reports the missing value.
--cpus sets the CPU count. Bare --memory values are MiB, and bare --disk values are GiB; 2G and 20G are also accepted. --disk sets the total disk capacity and cannot be smaller than the image requires.
Guest access and networking For a cloud image, --username names the initial administrator. --auth-type keys requires SSH public keys, supplied with repeatable --ssh-key options or --ssh-keys-file. Use --auth-type password with --password-file, or both with both password and keys. A password filename of - reads standard input. Do not pass a password as a command argument.
--hostname defaults to the new machine’s name. Use a fully qualified hostname when installing Virtualmin. --network selects a virtual network or bridge:NAME; it does not create that network. --address-mode dhcp uses automatic addressing. For static, supply addresses with prefixes, gateways where needed and --dns as a quoted list of server addresses. These settings configure the new guest through cloud-init.
Power and firmware The new machine starts by default, including when a template is selected. Use --no-start to leave it stopped. --autostart and --no-autostart control startup when the host boots. --firmware auto, efi or bios must be compatible with the selected image and host.
For an installer ISO, use --install-source iso and select an ISO image. Cloudmin creates an empty disk and attaches the installer. Complete operating system installation through the console; cloud-image account setup and automatic software installation do not apply to this mode.
Software and scripts --packages accepts a quoted, space-separated package list. --software virtualmin-gpl or virtualmin-pro installs Virtualmin after initial cloud-init setup. --virtualmin-bundle LAMP selects Apache, and LEMP selects Nginx; --virtualmin-type full or mini chooses the installation size. Virtualmin Pro also requires --license-serial-file and --license-file for its own license credentials.
When Enable Virtualmin installation? is disabled in Module Configuration, both review and creation reject requests to install Virtualmin. Templates that select Virtualmin directly or inherit it from Default Template are also blocked, even if the command overrides --software. Re-enable the setting to use them.
This setting does not affect package installation or setup scripts. Jobs submitted before it changed keep their settings.
Preparation and final setup scripts require Cloudmin Pro. --before-script-file or --after-script-file reads script contents; the corresponding --before-script-path or --after-script-path selects a file on the Cloudmin host. The scripts execute inside the guest as root, before package installation or after successful setup. Explicit script mode none clears an inherited script. Selecting guest software or scripts requires starting the guest.
Review and results --review validates the request and shows its resolved settings without creating a virtual machine. Omit that flag to submit the same settings for creation. A successful review does not reserve the name or resources against later changes.
--json returns the final job record, or the initial record with --no-wait. If the command loses its connection or times out while waiting, check list-jobs and get-job before submitting another creation. A software setup failure can leave the created machine available for inspection.
cloudmin create-system --name guest.example.com --template \ "Default Template" --plan "Default Plan" --auth-type keys \ --ssh-keys-file /root/guest-public-keys --review cloudmin create-system --name guest.example.com --template \ "Default Template" --plan "Default Plan" --auth-type keys \ --ssh-keys-file /root/guest-public-keys cloudmin create-system --name installer.example.com --install-source iso \ --image INSTALLER_IMAGE_ID --pool default --network default --cpus 2 \ --memory 2G --disk 20G Options:
--address-mode dhcp|static: Guest address configuration. --after-script-file file|-: Read guest script contents from a file. --after-script-mode none|file|inline: Guest script source (Cloudmin Pro). --after-script-path value: Guest script file on the Cloudmin host. --auth-type keys|password|both: Initial login authentication. --autostart | --no-autostart: Start when the host boots. --before-script-file file|-: Read guest script contents from a file. --before-script-mode none|file|inline: Guest script source (Cloudmin Pro). --before-script-path value: Guest script file on the Cloudmin host. --cpus number: Number of CPUs. --desc value: Description. --disk size: Total disk capacity; bare values use GiB. --dns value: Space- or comma-separated DNS servers. --firmware auto|efi|bios: Guest firmware. --gateway4 value: IPv4 gateway. --gateway6 value: IPv6 gateway. --host-ssh-key | --no-host-ssh-key: Create a managed host SSH key for the guest. --hostname value: Guest hostname; defaults to its name. --image ID|name: Imported or catalogue image ID or name. --install-source cloud|iso: Cloud image or installer ISO. --ipv4 value: Static IPv4 address with prefix. --ipv6 value: Static IPv6 address with prefix. --license-file file|-: Virtualmin Pro license key file, or - for stdin. --license-serial-file file|-: Virtualmin Pro serial file, or - for stdin. --mac value: Guest MAC address; omitted generates one. --memory size: Memory allocation; bare values use MiB. --name value: New virtual machine name. --network ID|name: Network key, UUID or name, or bridge:name. --packages value: Space-separated guest packages. --password-file file|-: Password file, or - for stdin. --plan ID|name: Plan ID or name. --pool ID|name: Destination storage pool ID or name. --require-fqdn | --no-require-fqdn: Require a fully qualified hostname. --review: Validate without creating. --software none|virtualmin-gpl|virtualmin-pro: Software to install. --ssh-key value: SSH public key; repeat for more keys. --ssh-keys-file file|-: File containing SSH public keys. --start | --no-start: Start after creation. --template ID|name: Template ID or name. --username value: Initial guest administrator account. --virtualmin-bundle LAMP|LEMP: Apache or Nginx stack. --virtualmin-postgres | --no-virtualmin-postgres: Install PostgreSQL. --virtualmin-ssl | --no-virtualmin-ssl: Request a hostname certificate. --virtualmin-type full|mini: Virtualmin installation size. --webmin-register | --no-webmin-register: Register the guest in the host Servers Index.
heading: Creates a virtual machine from a cloud image or installer ISO

content:
cloudmin clone-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--address-mode dhcp|static] [--auth-type keys|password|both] [--autostart | --no-autostart] [--confirm-license] [--confirm-unchanged] [--cpus number] [--desc value] [--disk size] [--dns value] [--gateway4 value] [--gateway6 value] [--host-ssh-key | --no-host-ssh-key] [--hostname value] [--ipv4 value] [--ipv6 value] [--mac value] [--memory size] [--mode prepared|unchanged] [--network ID|name] --new-name value [--nvram-mode fresh|copy] [--password-file file|-] [--plan ID|name] [--pool ID|name] [--require-fqdn | --no-require-fqdn] [--shutdown] [--ssh-key value]* [--ssh-keys-file file|-] [--start | --no-start] [--template ID|name] [--username value] Select the source with --name or --id, and give the destination an unused --new-name. Writable disks are copied to independent volumes with no backing files. The copy includes the source’s applications and data.
Prepared and unchanged copies The default --mode prepared configures a new guest identity, hostname, network and administrator access before boot. It requires one inspectable Linux installation, enabled cloud-init and one network interface. Supply the new login settings with --username, --auth-type and the password or public-key file options.
--mode unchanged retains guest settings and login credentials, but still resets the host ID and removes copied Virtualmin Pro credentials. It requires --confirm-unchanged and must remain stopped with automatic startup disabled. Review its network and access settings before starting it alongside the source.
Both modes require libguestfs with its Perl bindings and bsdtar on the host. Prepared cloning also needs YAML::XS. A source with Virtualmin Pro requires --confirm-license: copied license credentials are removed, and the clone needs its own license or a manual downgrade to GPL. The source’s credentials are unchanged.
Resources and source preparation Without explicit presets, the clone uses the source’s CPU count, memory, first-disk capacity, pool and network. --pool changes the destination pool. --disk can enlarge the first disk but cannot shrink it. A selected plan supplies resource defaults; a template supplies access, network and boot defaults. Template software installation and scripts are not run on the clone.
A running source needs a responding guest agent for a filesystem freeze and temporary snapshot. Alternatively, --shutdown stops it cleanly for copying and restarts it afterward. A source that was already stopped stays stopped. Allow storage for independent disk copies and temporary source disk growth.
For UEFI, --nvram-mode fresh creates new firmware variables. copy preserves them from a stopped source or requires --shutdown. The default is fresh variables when copying a running source without shutdown, and copied variables otherwise.
Completion Without a preset or explicit startup options, the clone stays stopped and automatic startup is disabled. Use --start for a prepared clone you want to boot after copying. An unchanged copy cannot start automatically.
The command waits for the job by default. --no-wait returns its ID. If copying or cleanup fails, use get-job and recover-job so Cloudmin can finish restoring the source and remove incomplete copies before releasing their reservations.
cloudmin clone-system --name source.example.com --new-name \ copy.example.com --auth-type keys --ssh-keys-file \ /root/guest-public-keys --no-start cloudmin clone-system --id MACHINE_UUID --new-name spare.example.com \ --mode unchanged --confirm-unchanged --no-start --no-autostart \ --shutdown Options:
--address-mode dhcp|static: Guest address configuration. --auth-type keys|password|both: Initial login authentication. --autostart | --no-autostart: Start when the host boots. --confirm-license: Acknowledge copied Virtualmin Pro credentials will be removed. --confirm-unchanged: Acknowledge that guest settings and credentials are retained. --cpus number: Number of CPUs. --desc value: Description. --disk size: Total disk capacity; bare values use GiB. --dns value: Space- or comma-separated DNS servers. --gateway4 value: IPv4 gateway. --gateway6 value: IPv6 gateway. --host-ssh-key | --no-host-ssh-key: Create a managed host SSH key for the guest. --hostname value: Guest hostname; defaults to its name. --id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --ipv4 value: Static IPv4 address with prefix. --ipv6 value: Static IPv6 address with prefix. --mac value: Guest MAC address; omitted generates one. --memory size: Memory allocation; bare values use MiB. --mode prepared|unchanged: Prepare a new identity or keep guest settings. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --network ID|name: Network key, UUID or name, or bridge:name. --new-name value: Destination virtual machine name. --nvram-mode fresh|copy: Create fresh firmware variables or copy them. --password-file file|-: Password file, or - for stdin. --plan ID|name: Plan ID or name. --pool ID|name: Destination storage pool ID or name. --require-fqdn | --no-require-fqdn: Require a fully qualified hostname. --shutdown: Cleanly stop the source while copying and restart it afterward. --ssh-key value: SSH public key; repeat for more keys. --ssh-keys-file file|-: File containing SSH public keys. --start | --no-start: Start after creation. --template ID|name: Template ID or name. --username value: Initial guest administrator account.
heading: Copies a virtual machine to independent disks

content:
cloudmin delete-system [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--disk value]* [--shutdown] --yes Removes the definition of the machine selected by --name or --id. --yes is required. Disk deletion is a separate choice: with no --disk options, every disk is kept, including the cloud-init seed. Repeat --disk with attached target names such as vda to permanently delete only those disks. Use list-disks to inspect the targets first.
A running machine requires --shutdown. If any writable disk is being kept, Cloudmin requests a clean shutdown and waits up to two minutes. If every writable disk is selected for deletion, it powers the machine off immediately. A failed or timed-out stop leaves the definition and disks intact; a delayed clean shutdown may still finish.
Remove native LVM snapshots before deleting the machine. Removing the machine also removes its libvirt snapshot and checkpoint metadata, firmware variable store and Cloudmin-managed SSH keys. Kept disks retain their backing chains, but the deleted machine’s snapshot list is no longer available. Selected disks’ private snapshot layers are deleted; shared layers and imported images remain protected.
Deletion runs as a job. The command waits for completion by default; --no-wait returns the job ID. Recovery can finish an interrupted deletion but cannot restore deleted data. Kept disks can be transferred or reattached, but they do not preserve the machine definition. Use a backup to preserve the complete machine.
cloudmin delete-system --name guest.example.com --yes cloudmin delete-system --name guest.example.com --shutdown --disk vda \ --disk vdb --yes Options:
--disk value: Attached disk target to delete; repeat for more disks. --id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --shutdown: Permit stopping a running guest. --yes: Confirm this operation.
heading: Deletes a virtual machine and only the selected disk targets

content:
cloudmin list-disks [--multiline | --json] [--name-only | --id-only] (--name name | --id uuid) Lists saved disk and removable-drive attachments for the machine selected by --name or --id. The default table shows the target, device type, role, format and path. Use it to distinguish writable disks, cloud-init seed media and CD/DVD drives before changing storage.
--target in disk commands refers to a guest device such as vda or sda, not a pool volume name, image ID or host path. --multiline or --json includes available volume details. --name-only and --id-only both print attachment targets, one per line.
This command shows storage attached to this machine. list-images lists reusable creation images instead. It does not inspect filesystems inside the guest.
cloudmin list-disks --name guest.example.com --multiline cloudmin list-disks --id MACHINE_UUID --id-only Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Lists a virtual machine’s disks and removable drives

content:
cloudmin create-disk [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--disk size] [--image ID|name] --pool ID|name Creates a disk in --pool and attaches it to the machine selected by --name or --id. Specify --disk for an empty disk, or --image for an independent copy of a ready imported image. File pools use QCOW2; LVM and LVM-thin pools use raw logical volumes. Catalogue entries must be imported before they can be used as additional disks.
--disk is the total capacity, in GiB when no suffix is given. With an image, omitting it keeps the image’s capacity; a larger value grows the copy, and a smaller value is rejected. The copied disk has no dependency on the original image.
Supported running guests can receive the disk live. A guest may still need to discover, partition, format and mount it. Existing snapshots or backup checkpoints can prevent adding disks. The command waits for the hardware job by default; --no-wait returns its ID. Use list-disks afterward to find the assigned target.
cloudmin create-disk --name guest.example.com --pool default --disk 50G cloudmin create-disk --id MACHINE_UUID --pool default --image \ IMPORTED_IMAGE_ID Options:
--disk size: Total disk capacity; bare values use GiB. --id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --image ID|name: Imported or catalogue image ID or name. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --pool ID|name: Destination storage pool ID or name.
heading: Creates and attaches a disk

content:
cloudmin attach-disk [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --pool ID|name --volume value Attaches an existing unused volume to the machine selected by --name or --id. --pool identifies its storage pool, and --volume is the volume’s name inside that pool, not a host filesystem path. Use this when reusing a disk kept by detach-disk or machine deletion.
The volume must be a supported raw or QCOW2 disk and pass ownership and dependency checks. Cloudmin protects imported images and disks referenced by other machines or storage. To create a separate copy of an imported image, use create-disk --image instead.
Supported running guests can receive the attachment live; Cloudmin does not mount or reconfigure filesystems inside the guest. Snapshots or checkpoints may block this change. The command waits for the hardware job unless --no-wait is supplied. list-disks shows the new target after completion.
cloudmin attach-disk --name guest.example.com --pool default --volume \ data.qcow2 Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --pool ID|name: Destination storage pool ID or name. --volume value: Volume name in the pool.
heading: Attaches an unused storage volume

content:
cloudmin detach-disk [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --target value Removes an attachment from the machine selected by --name or --id while keeping the storage volume and its data. --target is an attached device name from list-disks, such as vdb. This is different from delete-disk, which also removes the volume permanently.
Before detaching a disk in use, stop the guest applications using it and unmount it. For live removal, Cloudmin waits for the device to disappear from libvirt’s running definition before updating the saved configuration. If the guest does not acknowledge removal, the job can fail and require recovery.
Snapshots, checkpoints and unsupported devices can prevent detachment. The command waits for the job by default; --no-wait returns its ID. Use attach-disk with the original pool and volume name to attach the kept disk again.
cloudmin detach-disk --name guest.example.com --target vdb Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --target value: Attached disk target.
heading: Detaches a disk while keeping its data

content:
cloudmin delete-disk [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --target value --yes Detaches and permanently deletes one managed disk from the machine selected by --name or --id. --target must be an attached disk target from list-disks. --yes confirms deletion. Other disks and the machine itself are retained.
Use detach-disk when the data should be kept. Deletion cannot be undone by job recovery. Imported images, shared disks and disks with protected dependencies are refused. Snapshot or checkpoint history can also block the operation.
The operation runs as a job. By default, the command waits for completion; --no-wait returns its ID. If deletion is interrupted after detachment, use recover-job to let Cloudmin verify and finish removal of the same volume. This operation cannot be included in modify-system --changes-file.
cloudmin delete-disk --name guest.example.com --target vdb --yes Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --target value: Attached disk target. --yes: Confirm this operation.
heading: Detaches and permanently deletes one disk

content:
cloudmin resize-disk [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --disk size --target value Grows an attached disk on the machine selected by --name or --id. --target identifies the disk, and --disk is its new total capacity, not the amount to add. Bare sizes are GiB; for example, --disk 50G makes the disk 50 GiB.
Shrinking is not supported. Snapshots, checkpoints, shared storage or unsupported disk types can block growth. File disks can grow through libvirt while the guest runs. LVM and LVM-thin disks require the guest to be shut down first.
This changes virtual disk capacity only. Expand partitions, logical volumes and filesystems inside the guest separately. Completed growth cannot be rolled back, including when a later part of a job fails. The command waits for the job by default; --no-wait returns its ID.
cloudmin resize-disk --name guest.example.com --target vda --disk 50G Options:
--disk size: Total disk capacity; bare values use GiB. --id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --target value: Attached disk target.
heading: Grows a disk to the specified total capacity

content:
cloudmin insert-media [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --pool ID|name --target value --volume value Inserts an ISO volume into an existing CD/DVD drive on the machine selected by --name or --id. Find the drive target with list-disks, then supply that --target, the --pool containing the ISO and its --volume name. The volume name is not an image ID or a host path.
This changes the drive’s media; it does not create a drive, install an operating system or change boot order. For a stopped machine without a CD drive, modify-system --enable-live can add one. Set the desired boot device separately with modify-system --boot.
Supported guests can change media while running. The command waits for the hardware job unless --no-wait is supplied. Use eject-media to remove the media without deleting its storage volume.
cloudmin insert-media --name guest.example.com --target sda --pool \ default --volume installer.iso Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --pool ID|name: Destination storage pool ID or name. --target value: CD/DVD target. --volume value: ISO volume name.
heading: Inserts an ISO in an existing CD/DVD drive

content:
cloudmin eject-media [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --target value Ejects the media from the CD/DVD target on the machine selected by --name or --id. Find the target with list-disks. The drive stays attached, and the ISO volume remains in its storage pool for later use.
This does not detach a writable disk or change the saved boot order. Supported guests can eject media while running. The command waits for the hardware job by default; --no-wait returns the job ID.
cloudmin eject-media --name guest.example.com --target sda Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --target value: CD/DVD target.
heading: Ejects media without removing the drive

content:
cloudmin list-interfaces [--multiline | --json] [--name-only | --id-only] (--name name | --id uuid) Lists saved network interfaces for the machine selected by --name or --id. The default table shows each MAC address, source type, network or bridge, device model and link state. --multiline and --json include available bandwidth and other interface settings.
Interface commands identify an existing interface by its MAC address, not a guest name such as eth0. --name-only and --id-only therefore both print MAC addresses. Use list-networks to find network choices for adding or moving an interface.
These are virtual hardware settings. They do not show or rewrite the guest operating system’s complete network configuration.
cloudmin list-interfaces --name guest.example.com --multiline cloudmin list-interfaces --id MACHINE_UUID --id-only Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Lists a virtual machine’s network interfaces

content:
cloudmin add-interface [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--mac value] --network ID|name Adds a virtio network interface to the machine selected by --name or --id. --network selects an available virtual network or host bridge from list-networks. It accepts a network key, UUID, unambiguous name or bridge:NAME.
Cloudmin generates a MAC address unless --mac supplies one. The new interface can be attached live when the guest and host support it. The guest may need network configuration for the new device; this command does not rewrite its cloud-init seed or assign an IP address inside it.
The command waits for the job by default. --no-wait returns its ID. Use list-interfaces afterward to find the new MAC address and source.
cloudmin add-interface --name guest.example.com --network default cloudmin add-interface --id MACHINE_UUID --network bridge:br0 Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --mac value: Guest MAC address; omitted generates one. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --network ID|name: Network key, UUID or name, or bridge:name.
heading: Adds a virtio network interface

content:
cloudmin modify-interface [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--inbound-kib number] [--link up|down] --mac value [--network ID|name] [--outbound-kib number] Changes the interface identified by --mac on the machine selected by --name or --id. Find the MAC address with list-interfaces. Omitted fields keep their current values; --mac selects the interface and does not change its address.
--network moves the interface to another available virtual network or host bridge. --link down disconnects its virtual link while retaining the interface; --link up reconnects it. Network changes can interrupt the guest’s connection and may require new addressing inside the guest. Cloudmin does not rewrite guest networking or its cloud-init seed.
--inbound-kib and --outbound-kib set average bandwidth limits in KiB per second, not kilobits. A value of zero removes that direction’s limit. Live support depends on the interface and network backend.
The command waits for the hardware job by default; --no-wait returns its ID. This command does not change the interface model or MAC address.
cloudmin modify-interface --name guest.example.com --mac \ 52:54:00:12:34:56 --network bridge:br0 cloudmin modify-interface --name guest.example.com --mac \ 52:54:00:12:34:56 --inbound-kib 10240 --outbound-kib 10240 Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --inbound-kib number: Inbound average KiB/s; zero removes the limit. --link up|down: Interface link state. --mac value: Guest MAC address; omitted generates one. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --network ID|name: Network key, UUID or name, or bridge:name. --outbound-kib number: Outbound average KiB/s; zero removes the limit.
heading: Changes an interface’s network, link or bandwidth

content:
cloudmin delete-interface [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --mac value Removes the interface identified by --mac from the machine selected by --name or --id. Use list-interfaces to find its MAC address. This removes the virtual device; it does not delete the host network or bridge.
Removing an interface can disconnect the guest, including an SSH session using that interface. To disconnect it temporarily while keeping its configuration, use modify-interface --link down instead. Guest network configuration is not rewritten automatically.
Supported devices can be removed live. The command waits for the hardware job unless --no-wait is supplied. If live removal fails or is interrupted, inspect the job before retrying; the guest may acknowledge the removal later.
cloudmin delete-interface --name guest.example.com --mac 52:54:00:12:34:56 Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --mac value: Guest MAC address; omitted generates one. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Removes a network interface

content:
cloudmin list-snapshots [--multiline | --json] [--name-only | --id-only] [--name name | --id uuid] With no machine selector, lists snapshots across the host. Supply --name or --id to limit the list to one virtual machine. --id is the machine UUID; a restore point’s own identifier is passed as --snapshot to restore or delete commands.
The default table shows snapshot ID, machine, label, state and creation time. --multiline or --json provides detailed records. --id-only and --name-only both print snapshot IDs, since labels need not be unique.
Cloudmin can show externally created snapshots, but it may not support restoring or deleting them. Cloudmin-managed snapshots contain disk state and saved hardware configuration, not running memory. They remain on the host’s storage and do not replace backups stored elsewhere.
cloudmin list-snapshots cloudmin list-snapshots --name guest.example.com --multiline cloudmin list-snapshots --id MACHINE_UUID --id-only Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name.
heading: Lists snapshots for the host or one virtual machine

content:
cloudmin create-snapshot [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--desc value] --label value [--mode prepared|unprepared] [--restart] [--shutdown] Creates a disk restore point for the machine selected by --name or --id. --label is required; --desc adds an optional description. The label describes the restore point, while its generated ID is used for later restore and deletion.
The default --mode prepared uses the guest agent to freeze filesystems briefly when the machine is running. --shutdown permits a clean shutdown when the agent is unavailable. It does not force a shutdown when agent preparation is available. A stopped guest does not need an agent. Add --restart to start the machine after a successful snapshot if it was stopped for the operation.
--mode unprepared captures a running guest’s disks without freezing filesystems. The captured data is crash-consistent: applications may need recovery when it is restored, as they would after a sudden power loss. Neither mode saves running memory or external services. Filesystem freezing does not replace application-specific backup steps.
Snapshots support private raw or QCOW2 files and managed LVM disks. A snapshot cannot mix file and LVM disks. Cloudmin limits managed restore points to 20 per machine. Snapshot history restricts disk attachment, removal and growth until that history is removed.
Live LVM snapshots briefly pause the guest and require direct I/O or synchronous disk caching. Disks created by Cloudmin use direct I/O. Standard LVM snapshots reserve space for a full disk’s changes, while thin snapshots share their pool. Restoring an LVM snapshot requires temporary space under /var/tmp for the largest disk’s full capacity plus 256 MiB.
The command waits for the job by default; --no-wait returns its ID. Find the completed restore point with list-snapshots. Snapshot layers use the same storage as the guest, so maintain separate backups for host or disk failure.
cloudmin create-snapshot --name guest.example.com --label before-upgrade cloudmin create-snapshot --id MACHINE_UUID --label maintenance \ --shutdown --restart Options:
--desc value: Description. --id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --label value: Snapshot label. --mode prepared|unprepared: Snapshot preparation mode. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --restart: Start after success. --shutdown: Permit clean shutdown if the guest agent is unavailable.
heading: Creates a disk snapshot

content:
cloudmin restore-snapshot [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--restart] [--shutdown] --snapshot value --yes Restores the machine selected by --name or --id to the restore point identified by --snapshot. Use list-snapshots to obtain that ID. --yes confirms replacing current disk contents and saved hardware settings with the snapshot’s state.
The machine must be stopped, or --shutdown must permit a clean shutdown first. Add --restart to start it after a successful restore. Without that flag, it remains stopped. A failed clean shutdown does not become a forced power-off.
The restore does not resume the old running memory state. Changes made after the restore point can be lost, including files and application data. Other restore points are retained, but only supported Cloudmin-managed history can be restored.
The command waits for the background job by default. --no-wait returns its ID. After success, inspect the guest and its applications before treating the restored service as ready.
cloudmin restore-snapshot --name guest.example.com --snapshot \ SNAPSHOT_ID --yes cloudmin restore-snapshot --id MACHINE_UUID --snapshot SNAPSHOT_ID \ --shutdown --restart --yes Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --restart: Start after restoring. --shutdown: Permit clean shutdown before restoring. --snapshot value: Snapshot ID. --yes: Confirm this operation.
heading: Restores a saved snapshot

content:
cloudmin delete-snapshot [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) --snapshot value --yes Removes the restore point identified by --snapshot from the machine selected by --name or --id. --yes is required. Use list-snapshots to select the snapshot ID, rather than its label.
Deleting a file snapshot merges its disk layers. Deleting an LVM snapshot removes its saved volumes. Both preserve the machine’s current disk contents and hardware settings. The selected restore point is no longer available afterward.
History dependencies can prevent deletion, and external snapshot history cannot be changed through this command. Merges may take time and require free space. The command waits for the job unless --no-wait is supplied. If a merge is interrupted, use get-job and recover-job; deleting layer files by hand can damage the remaining disk chain.
cloudmin delete-snapshot --name guest.example.com --snapshot SNAPSHOT_ID \ --yes Options:
--id uuid: Source virtual machine UUID. --name name: Source virtual machine name. --snapshot value: Snapshot ID. --yes: Confirm this operation.
heading: Deletes a snapshot while keeping current disk data

content:
cloudmin list-backups [--multiline | --json] [--name-only | --id-only] Lists completed backup archives recorded by this Cloudmin host. The table includes backup job ID, source machine name, creation time, archive size and destination. Use the ID with inspect-backup --backup before restoring.
This is the local backup inventory, not a scan of every destination. An archive removed outside Cloudmin can still have a record here; inspection verifies that it is available and usable. Backups created on another host can be inspected by supplying their destination and filename directly.
--multiline and --json show detailed records without destination credentials. --name-only prints source machine names, which can repeat across backups. --id-only prints backup job IDs, not virtual machine UUIDs.
cloudmin list-backups --multiline cloudmin list-backups --id-only
heading: Lists completed backup archives

content:
cloudmin backup-systems [--multiline | --json] [--no-wait] (--name name | --id uuid) [--compression | --no-compression] [--dest-access-file file|-] [--dest-account value] [--dest-bucket value] [--dest-ca-file value] [--dest-endpoint value] [--dest-host value] [--dest-key-file value] --dest-mode local|ssh|s3|gcs|azure|bb|dropbox|drive [--dest-password-file file|-] --dest-path value [--dest-port number] [--dest-project value] [--dest-refresh-token-file file|-] [--dest-region value] [--dest-secret-file file|-] [--dest-session-token-file file|-] [--dest-subscription value] [--dest-user value] [--shutdown] Creates one complete virtual machine backup per command. Select the machine with --name or --id. The archive includes writable disks, the saved hardware definition and supported firmware state. It retains the guest’s identity and login settings for restoration.
Guest preparation and storage A running guest normally needs a responding agent to freeze filesystems while Cloudmin takes a temporary snapshot. --shutdown instead stops it cleanly for copying and restarts it afterward. A source that was already stopped stays stopped. Temporary file snapshot layers are merged back before completion; temporary LVM snapshots are removed.
